judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional rule for 'Contractor' where separate contracts are awarded; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1.1 and 5.1.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Deemed necessary after a joint review and mutual agreement' and the schedule then constituting 'the schedules to be used' is workable but leaves revision authority diffuse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4-3.10.5 make the Construction Schedule a Contract Document revised at design phases, a different amendment route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deems the Owner subject to the same obligations as the Contractor when using its own forces; broad but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 disclaims any Owner responsibility for means, methods and safety 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner', which pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable opportunity' for introduction and storage; a modest standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.13.1 and 6.1.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Failure to report converts to an acknowledgment of fitness 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable' — a deemed admission bounded only by discoverability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 3.2.1-3.2.3 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b); consistent in approach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mutual responsibility for delay, improperly timed activities, damage and defective construction; broadly worded but symmetrical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.3.10's waiver of consequential damages limits what can be recovered under this clause, a relationship that must be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Damage wrongfully caused' is the only elastic term in a short duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to 10.2.5; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extends 3.14 duties to the Owner and separate contractors; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.14 and 6.1.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lets the Owner clean up and the Architect 'allocate the cost among those responsible' without a stated standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.3 makes debris removal a reimbursable Cost of the Work, so allocation could double up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned sentence is fragmented, though the rule (changes by Change Order, Construction Change Directive or order for a minor change) is recognisable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 says a change in the Contract Sum or Time 'shall be accomplished only by Change Order' except as permitted in 7.3 and 9.7.1, omitting 7.4 minor changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a Change Order as prepared by the Architect and signed by Owner, Contractor and Architect; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.4.1 has the Owner issue a Change Order deducting correction costs without Contractor signature, and 7.3.5 converts a signed Directive into a Change Order — different formation routes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision survives only as a fragment in this copy, so the methods it lists cannot be read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its content is supplied by 7.3.3 and Agreement 6.1-6.3; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned definition of a Construction Change Directive is garbled, though the concept (Architect-prepared, Owner-signed, change before agreement on adjustment) is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 preserves Paragraph 7.3 as an exception, so Directives remain a route to adjustment despite the Change-Order-only rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four alternative bases including 'cost to be determined in a manner agreed upon by the parties and a mutually acceptable fixed or percentage fee' — an agreement to agree inside a pricing menu.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.2 and 6.3 redefine 'cost' and 'fee' for these very clauses, differently for subcontracts and for the Guaranteed Maximum Price, so the method chosen changes meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires prompt performance of the directed change while allowing disagreement on the adjustment; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 expressly preserves 7.3, so the two are reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned sentence is broken but the rule (a Directive signed by the Contractor becomes a Change Order) is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.1.3.1 and 7.2.1; supports the Change-Order-only regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual net cost as confirmed by the Architect' and figuring overhead and profit 'on the basis of net increase, if any' are precise but arithmetic-sensitive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.3 substitutes the Contractor's Fee for 'a reasonable allowance for overhead and profit' in these very provisions, so the deletion credit must be computed under a different vocabulary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interim determinations for monthly certification pending final determination; intricate but internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.7.1 expressly incorporates 7.3.8 for amounts not in dispute; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Agreement on adjustments is effective immediately and recorded by Change Order; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.1.3.1 and 7.2.3's finality rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor changes ... not involving adjustment in the Contract Sum or extension of the Contract Time and not inconsistent with the intent of the Contract Documents' is a boundary that is argued about after the fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits changes only by Change Order 'except as permitted in Paragraph 7.3 and Paragraph 9.7.1' — notably not 7.4 — so this authority may have been written out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Contract Time; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on Agreement 4.3 and Addendum 4.3 [Revised], which state the period differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition tied to the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.1 [Revised] makes the date 'July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits', so the 'date established in the Agreement' is itself conditional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and precise: the date certified by the Architect under 9.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.4's bonus turns on the Work being 'determined to be substantially complete' without saying by whom, which this definition may or may not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Day' means calendar day unless otherwise stated; definitional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the day counts throughout Articles 4, 9 and 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Time limits ... are of the essence' plus a deemed confirmation that the Contract Time is reasonable; short and potent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement inserted no liquidated damages, Addendum 4.4 adds an undetermined early-completion bonus, and Addendum 4.3 substitutes a fixed date — so the time regime is assembled from disparate parts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extract runs two subparagraphs together and includes an insurance-effective-date rule plus a five-day notice for filing mortgages and liens; readable but cluttered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1 leaves the Owner's time to file mortgages and mechanic's liens blank, and Article 16's insurance requirements are also blank, so the trigger dates are unstated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceed expeditiously with adequate forces' is a soft performance standard, but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by Addendum Article 2 [Revised] and Supplementary Condition 3.10.4; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of excusable delay causes closing with 'other causes beyond the Contractor's control' and 'other causes which the Architect determines may justify delay' — an open catch-all whose reach against the specifics is the classic problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4 bars separate increases for concurrent or interrelated causes and for delays due to the Contractor's fault, narrowing this grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line routing of time claims to Paragraph 4.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplemented by Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3-4.3.7.4; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract Sum is stated in the Agreement' — but the Agreement states it as a formula (Cost of the Work plus Fee), not an amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.1 leaves the Guaranteed Maximum Price as 'N/A', so the 'total amount payable' this definition assumes is nowhere fixed, while 9.5.1.5 and 14.2.4 speak of an 'unpaid balance of the Contract Sum'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At least ten days before the date established for each progress payment' with notarisation 'if required' and such data 'as the Owner or Architect may require'; workable but open-ended at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.3's application and payment dates are partly blank or garbled, and Addendum 12.1.4 adds documentation requirements, so the application timetable is spread across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits payment requests for authorised Directives and interim determinations; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.3.8 and Agreement 12.1.7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions payment for stored materials on 'procedures satisfactory to the Owner' — an unmeasured satisfaction standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2 impose their own advance-approval and written-location requirements for the same items.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the best of the Contractor's knowledge, information and belief' qualifies a warranty of clear title; the qualifier is the soft part.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) requires lien waivers with each application and 12.2.2 requires a lien-free endorsement, which press harder than this qualified warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A seven-day certification deadline with a defined alternative; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 expressly supersedes 9.4.1's time periods for final payment, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully hedged representation language with an enumerated list of what certification does not imply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.9 states a parallel reliance disclaimer for cost-plus applications; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seven enumerated grounds for withholding, several of them open-textured ('reasonable evidence', 'persistent failure'), used to justify a discretionary withholding 'to the extent reasonably necessary to protect the Owner'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ground .5 (evidence the Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum) presupposes a fixed sum that this cost-plus contract with an 'N/A' GMP does not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single restorative sentence; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.5.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment 'in the manner and within the time provided in the Contract Documents'; the content is elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.3's payment dates are partly blank, so this obligation borrows an incomplete timetable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pay-when-paid style obligation to Subcontractors 'upon receipt of payment from the Owner'; standard AIA language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1's joint-check right and Addendum 12.1.4(a)-(b) alter the flow of subcontract payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclaimer of Owner obligations to Subcontractors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1 permits joint payments while expressly disclaiming any resulting obligation, so the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-references in this copy ('Subparagraphs 9.6.2, 9.6.3 and 9.4') appear corrupted, leaving the incorporated treatment uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on 9.6.2 and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1; substantively consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment or occupancy is not acceptance of nonconforming Work; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.3 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It creates a holding obligation 'unless the Contractor provides ... a payment bond in the full penal sum' and then disclaims separate accounts, fiduciary liability, tort liability and punitive damages — a trust that expressly is not a trust.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 of the Agreement is blank as to bonds, so the exception may be inoperative, and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1's joint payments bypass the holding mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-help stop-work right on seven days' notice with recovery of 'reasonable costs of shut-down, delay and start-up, plus interest as provided for in the Contract Documents' — the interest rate blank and the cost categories are both loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.3.10 waives consequential damages, Agreement 14.2 leaves the interest rate unfilled, and Agreement 12.1.3's payment dates are garbled, so the trigger and the remedy both depend on unsettled terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently complete in accordance with the Contract Documents so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use' is the definition parties most often litigate, and 'sufficiently' is doing all the work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.3 fixes a Substantial Completion date and Addendum 4.4 pays a bonus for early substantial completion, so this definition drives both a deadline and a payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected' with failure to list not altering responsibility; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.8.3-9.8.4 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inspection and re-inspection procedure in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.8.1-9.8.4; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner participation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Certificate fixes the date, allocates responsibilities and starts warranties 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate' — a document that can rewrite the warranty start date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12.2.2's one-year correction period and 13.7.1's limitation accrual both run from Substantial Completion, so the Certificate's content has knock-on effects.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment of retainage on acceptance and consent of surety, 'adjusted for Work that is incomplete'; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's 12.1.7.3 states retainage as 'N/A' while Addendum 12.1.7.3 sets five percent and 12.1.8 sets ten percent for Subcontractors, so what retainage is released is unclear.
